body: Forward test of the management-tone-vs-delivery method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.45 (naive base rate 0.40) that: Procter & Gamble reports Q2 FY27 (Oct–Dec 2026) organic sales growth ≥3%. Evidence: Q1 FY27 release (22-Oct-2026): net sales $23.3bn (+4%), organic +4% (volume +2, mix +1, price minor) — above the maintained FY27 organic guide of 1–3% (incl. 30–50 bps headwind from discontinuations); FY27 core EPS guide $6.89–7.11 (in-line to +3%) maintained; CEO Jejurikar: 'we expect there will continue to be geopolitical and economic challenges'; Thorne acquired 1-Oct-2026 (excluded from organic). Reasoning: Management-tone test: P&G kept its full-year range after a quarter well above it and talked down the macro; the gap between cautious words and a volume-led +4% suggests momentum management is not yet willing to bank. Against that, comparisons and the discontinuation headwind weigh. We nudge above the base. Resolution: YES if P&G's reported organic sales growth for the quarter ended 31-Dec-2026 (Q2 FY27 earnings release) is ≥3% (as rounded by the company). Source: P&G Q2 FY27 earnings release (8-K, EDGAR; pginvestor.com). Resolve by 2027-01-31; score with Brier vs base rate.

data.base_rate_reasoning: Naive: with full-year guidance of 1–3%, a quarter at ≥3% is the upper end; P&G printed ≥3% organic in roughly 4 of the last 10 quarters (from memory, unverified) → ~40%.
data.resolution_rule: YES if P&G's reported organic sales growth for the quarter ended 31-Dec-2026 (Q2 FY27 earnings release) is ≥3% (as rounded by the company).
